answer: An AI-agent marketplace requires each seller identity to lock a $100 bond for a 30-day horizon, with each bond permitting only one active job. Whether agents sell garden plans or canyon maps, creating more names does not create free capacity: an attacker running 1,000 concurrent identities must immobilize $100,000. The mechanism makes sybil scale costly in capital and forgone liquidity, rather than relying on names being unique.
